grounding.quote:
Published world-model truth should be:

- immutable per cut
- reviewable by diff
- traceable to evidence
- superseded by explicit later cuts rather than silently overwritten
Both should remain append-only and replayable.

constraints.statement: Published world-model truth should be immutable per cut, diff-reviewable, evidence-traceable and explicitly superseded rather than silently overwritten. Both ledgers should remain append-only and replayable. A later database is a query complement, not constitutional publication authority.

grounding.quote:
The method does not assume one source per attribute. It assumes one lawful
claim record per accepted attribute fact.

Every entry should be a fully qualified claim, potentially including:

- a value or measured quantity
- a rule or constraint
- a classification
- a topology or relation claim
- provenance and authority information
- effective, observed, and publication coordinates

constraints.statement: Every entry should be fully qualified, potentially carrying values/measurements, rules/constraints, classification, topology/relations, provenance/authority and effective/observed/publication coordinates. One or more evidence surfaces may support it: documents for declared semantics/policy, code for derivation/invariants, data for observed state/emitted values. The method assumes one lawful claim record per accepted attribute fact, not one source per attribute.

grounding.quote:
One demonstrated failed admission obligation remains visible alongside a
different unresolved obligation. No sparse-publication allowance removes an
applicable failed requirement. Publication proceeds only under the owning
admission predicate and authority, with tolerated ambiguity still reported.

An entity cut is admissible when its identity, boundary, authority, state,
evidence, treatment, covariance, and ambiguity are explicit, traceable, and
discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence altitude proportional to
the claim.

That is the whole constitutional test. It binds what must be true of a
published cut. It does not prescribe how a builder establishes it.

"Explicit" admits three lawful values on every surface: a stated value, stated
absence, or stated non-applicability with its reason. A cut whose entity has no
adjacent-domain treatment says so; it does not manufacture one. This keeps the
predicate whole without adding evidence machinery.

constraints.statement: Admissibility binds all eight surfaces—identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance, ambiguity—to explicitness, traceability and discrimination proportional to the claim. Explicitness permits a stated value, supported stated absence, or supported non-applicability with reason; missing treatment is declared rather than manufactured. The consumer binds the predicate and required evidence and conjoins component results. Unexamined properties remain unresolved; demonstrated failures remain visible alongside unresolved obligations. Publication requires the owning predicate and authority and reports tolerated ambiguity. This test does not prescribe a builder technique.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced result-conjunction definition is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Boundary is interventional in character, not structural. A cut that states its
boundary only as a set of source fields has made a weaker claim than one that
states the reinterpretations under which identity survives, and should be read
as such.

"Discriminated from plausible alternatives" means the cut states why this
boundary rather than a nearby one the operating model would treat differently.
The claim carries its own discrimination; a stronger claim needs stronger
discrimination.

constraints.statement: A cut states why its boundary differs from a nearby boundary the operating model would treat differently; stronger claims need stronger discrimination. Adjoint round-trip supplies semantic discrimination analogous to geometric boundary testing. Where intervention is possible, interventional evidence discriminates more strongly than declarative evidence, and the cut should identify its evidence kind. A field-set-only boundary is weaker than a boundary stating identity-preserving reinterpretations and should be read accordingly.

conditions: An entity cut is published.

grounding.quote:
A published entity cut makes the eight admissibility surfaces — identity,
boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance, and ambiguity —
visible and traceable, each as a stated value, stated absence, or stated
non-applicability, and records the basis on which identity was discriminated.

Cuts are immutable. Revising identity or boundary produces a new cut that
supersedes the prior one.

Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas, and storage topology are consumer
realization. This method requires that the published surfaces survive; it does
not select the form they are stored in.

constraints.statement: Expose all eight admissibility surfaces visibly and traceably as value, absence or non-applicability and record the identity-discrimination basis. Cuts are immutable; identity or boundary revision creates a superseding cut. Consumer-selected carriers, layouts, schemas and topology must preserve the published surfaces.

conditions: The representation-substrate specialization applies.

grounding.quote:
The declared representation space is part of the overlay. An identity
direction is uninterpretable without the space it lives in, and directions
computed in different spaces do not compose.

constraints.statement: The declared representation space is part of the overlay; an identity direction is uninterpretable without it. Directions computed in different spaces do not compose. The directional interventional framework governs both construction and minimum published storage.

conditions: Constructing an overlay for a candidate in the applicable representation space.

grounding.quote:
For a candidate object, assemble attribute-ledger evidence across
context variation together with evidence for at least one null peer:

- multiple contexts in which the candidate is instantiated
- a null-peer instance: a structurally similar thing that lacks the
  candidate's identity content, observed in the same contexts
- paired ledger entries covering `(candidate, context)` and
  `(null, context)` so identity-carrying signal can be separated from
  context-carrying signal

The paired evidence is the raw material of the cut. The ledger entries
remain distributed; they are not the object.

constraints.statement: Collect attribute-ledger evidence in multiple candidate contexts with at least one structurally similar null peer lacking the candidate's identity content in those same contexts. Pair candidate/context and null/context entries to separate identity from context signal. Entries remain distributed raw material, not the object.

conditions: Assessing a candidate identity direction for overlay publication.
exceptions: The underlying entity cut remains lawful and publishable without the overlay.

grounding.quote:
A candidate identity direction is accepted only if projection along
it preserves object identity under held-out treatments. The builder
must record at least one acceptable verification:

- α-sweep: apply `x − α · d` on held-out contexts, show expected
  identity shift and its saturation behaviour
- transplant: apply `x + α · d` to null-peer instances, show
  identity acquisition
- boundary test: overwrite attributes outside the projection support
  and show identity survives (this is what discriminates geometric
  blanket from set-membership blanket)

A direction that has no acceptable verification is a candidate, not an
accepted overlay. Publishing an unverified direction is a violation of
the Representation Law. The underlying entity cut remains lawful and
publishable without the overlay.

constraints.statement: Acceptance requires identity preservation under held-out treatment and at least one recorded acceptable verification: α-sweep x − α·d showing expected identity shift and saturation; transplant x + α·d to null peers showing identity acquisition; or overwriting attributes outside projection support showing identity survives. No acceptable verification leaves a candidate; publishing an unverified direction violates the source's Representation Law. Supported preservation satisfies, a counterexample falsifies, unrun/inconclusive treatment is indeterminate with performance retained, unusable representation/fixture/interpretation is invalid_basis, and established scope/capability shortfall is out_of_frame. Candidate/accepted status follows assessment plus other publication obligations, is not itself a verdict and does not establish formal Markov-blanket closure.
constraints.uncertainty: Representation Law and Epistemic Status Of The Construct are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: The candidate appears in multiple contexts.

grounding.quote:
For candidates that appear in multiple contexts, decompose the
attribute evidence into:

- **invariant core**: attributes whose contribution to the identity
  direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts
- **context coat**: attributes selected by the specific context,
  carrying contextual reinterpretation rather than identity per se

Both are evidence. The core carries identity. The coat carries
treatment. The coat/core ratio is a characterization, not a quality
metric.

constraints.statement: Decompose evidence into invariant core—attributes with identity-direction contribution stable across ≥ N of N contexts—and context coat—context-selected attributes carrying contextual reinterpretation. Both are evidence; core carries identity, coat carries treatment, and coat/core ratio characterizes rather than grades quality.
constraints.uncertainty: N and the operational criterion for stable contribution are not specified here.

conditions: Before overlay publication.

grounding.quote:
Assess uniqueness and transfer as separate predicates on the declared candidate,
null peers, contexts and representation, using the selected comparison and
observation rules. Evidence meeting each rule is satisfied for that predicate;
a demonstrated failure is falsified; an unrun or inconclusive comparison is
indeterminate with actual performance retained. Invalid basis and established
scope/capability shortfall retain their core diagnoses. Core size alone supplies
neither failure nor success. Conjoin the required null-peer and treatment
results for overlay-publication eligibility, retaining failed comparisons and
missing coverage. That eligibility is distinct from ordinary entity-cut
admissibility and from formal conditional-independence closure.

constraints.statement: Discriminate from incidental clusters using null peers. Core sizes overlapping null-peer sizes are expected and acceptable, never diagnostic. Identity-loaded core attributes should be unique among null peers and the direction should transfer more cleanly than a random representation diagonal. Failure on the required uniqueness/transfer tests prevents lawful Markov-object standing despite internally consistent invariants. Assess uniqueness and transfer separately against declared candidate, peers, contexts, representation and selected comparison/observation rules: meeting a rule satisfies; demonstrated failure falsifies; unrun/inconclusive comparison is indeterminate with performance retained; invalid basis and established scope/capability shortfall retain their diagnoses. Conjoin required null-peer and treatment results, retaining failures and missing coverage. Overlay eligibility is distinct from entity-cut admissibility and formal conditional-independence closure.
constraints.uncertainty: Specific comparison rules and thresholds are selected elsewhere.

conditions: An overlay is published.
exceptions: The effective coordinate α is required where applicable.

grounding.quote:
An overlay is an immutable projection. Revising the identity direction —
because new contexts, new evidence, or a re-fitted representation space
became available — produces a new overlay that supersedes the prior one.
A change of representation space changes every direction expressed in it
and is therefore a supersession even when no ledger entry changed. Prior
overlays are never mutated in place (see Publication Law).

- **representation space**: the declared space and attribute basis the
  direction is expressed in, versioned so a later re-fit is detectable
- **identity direction**: the projection (representation-space
  vector or equivalent geometric description)
- **attribute evidence**: core + coat, traced to ledger entries
- **verification record**: treatments used, outcomes observed,
  held-out contexts evaluated
- **boundary characterization**: projection support on which identity
  was preserved under treatment
- **null-peer comparison**: what similar things were tested, what
  was accepted, what was rejected
- **effective coordinate**: α along direction for this instance,
  where applicable

constraints.statement: Expose at least versioned representation space/attribute basis, geometric direction, core+coat evidence traced to ledger entries, verification treatments/outcomes/held-out contexts, identity-preserving projection support, null peers tested and accepted/rejected results, and applicable instance α. Direction revision creates a superseding overlay. Representation-space change supersedes every affected direction even without ledger changes; prior overlays are never mutated in place.

grounding.quote:
The stored overlay is not a row in a table and not a membership list.
It is a package attached to its entity cut:

- the declared representation space and its version
- the geometric object (identity direction and projection support)
- the distributed evidence (pointers into the attribute ledger)
- the verification trace (treatments, contexts, outcomes)
- the provenance and authority record (who accepted, on what
  assurance basis)
- the supersession record (which overlay this replaces, if any)

A storage layout that loses any of these surfaces is not a lawful
Markov-object storage layout. Query planes and projection surfaces
derived from stored cuts are downstream conveniences and do not
substitute for this storage shape.

constraints.statement: Store an entity-cut-attached package, not merely a table row or membership list: representation/version; direction/support; distributed ledger pointers; treatment/context/outcome trace; accepting party and assurance basis; and predecessor overlay, if any. Losing any surface makes the layout unlawful. Derived query planes/projections do not substitute.

grounding.quote:
Builder projects may work a bounded source-object set repeatedly until the
resulting attribute ledger is judged sufficiently saturated for publication.

Sufficient saturation means:

- materially important attributes have traceable support
- remaining gaps are explicit ambiguities rather than silent misses
- the resulting object cut is stable enough to publish and supersede later if
  needed

Sparse first publication remains lawful. Silent unsupported attribute creation
does not.

constraints.statement: Construction is iterative; builders may revisit a bounded source-object set until judged sufficiently saturated. Saturation means traceable support for materially important attributes, explicit ambiguity for remaining gaps, and a cut stable enough to publish and later supersede if needed. Sparse first publication remains lawful; silent unsupported attribute creation does not.
constraints.uncertainty: The concrete saturation judgment and threshold are not supplied.

exceptions: There is no generic translation exception to the prohibition on composing directions from different representation spaces.

grounding.quote:
A candidate geometric claim cannot acquire established standing through
composition or averaging. Directions in different representation spaces do not
compose; changing that space supersedes the prior overlay. This domain policy
admits no generic translation exception. Claims of adjunction or equivalence
require the evidence in [Orthogonal descriptions](FOUNDATIONS.md#orthogonal-descriptions).

Prefer a federated world-model mesh to a flattened central model. Detailed
mesh topology may remain product-local while the line is developed.
Method-level mesh law should be ratified only once the reusable node and edge
model is stable; stability alone supplies no ratification authority.

constraints.statement: Do not build a central monolith first. Compose local published artifacts/cuts under the library composition contract, binding participating cuts, exact bases, treatment predicates, fragment authorities, bounded-context meanings, declared loss and ambiguity; required checks conjoin actual claims. Higher-order publication retains local artifacts and identities. Composition/averaging cannot promote candidate geometric standing. Different-space directions do not compose; space changes supersede overlays. Adjunction/equivalence require referenced evidence. Prefer federation; topology may remain product-local during development. Method-level mesh law should await stable reusable nodes/edges, and stability grants no ratification authority.
constraints.uncertainty: Composition contract, core conjunction and Orthogonal descriptions are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Reliance on a projection for a declared source-to-consumer claim applies
[Faithful projection](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#faithful-projection) with that
kernel as source. Bind the material source relations, exact selectors and
declared loss required by that use. Publication alone establishes neither that
fidelity claim nor new semantic authority.

Tables, schemas, APIs, mapping documents and covariant transforms are forms
over that kernel. Prefer `world model -> API contract -> schema contract`
because the API commonly carries more domain meaning than a bare schema.
Query and traversal are downstream delivery capabilities. Their delivery
importance does not transfer ownership of the semantic kernel.

constraints.statement: All projections should remain traceable to governing objects, evidence, treatments, covariance edges, adjoints and applicable temporal references. Reliance for a declared source-to-consumer claim applies Faithful projection with the kernel as source and binds material relations, exact selectors and required declared loss. Publication alone proves neither fidelity nor new authority. Tables, schemas, APIs, mapping documents and covariant transforms are forms over the kernel; prefer world model → API contract → schema contract. Query/traversal delivery importance does not transfer kernel ownership.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced Faithful projection contract is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The high-volume data plane consists of deterministic executable artifacts
compiled from accepted semantic understanding.

The build tenant supplies the computational binding under
[Spec Method](SPEC_METHOD.md#what-how-and-work-carriers).
Human source interpretation, machine transformation and
mixed assurance can realize different operations in the same construction.
The selected means preserve the same governing predicates; a human title or a
tool name does not supply a missing contract. Bulk execution retains the
deterministic compilation obligation where this profile applies.

constraints.statement: The semantic control plane comprises published domain artifacts, composed models, treatments/covariance/adjoints and epistemic correspondence/ranking/ambiguity overlays. The bulk data plane uses deterministic executables compiled from accepted understanding, with build-tenant computational binding. Human interpretation, machine transformation and mixed assurance may realize different operations while preserving governing predicates; titles/tool names do not supply missing contracts. Where this profile applies, bulk execution retains deterministic compilation. World-model artifacts carry semantic truth, epistemic overlays probability/uncertainty, and compiled artifacts deterministic behavior: a plane split, not a truth split. LLMs/probabilistic systems belong primarily in semantic control and should aid comprehension, candidate alignment, ambiguity reduction and correspondence ranking; they should not execute large-scale movement row by row when accepted understanding can be compiled.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced computational-binding contract is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The proof obligation is practical:

build the world model once, then show that the same semantic substrate can emit
the legacy artifacts the organization expects and the richer covariant outputs
the method makes possible.

Where the line is mature enough, the proof should also show that accepted
semantic understanding can be compiled into deterministic executable pipelines
without losing the traceability and challengeability of the governing world
model.

constraints.statement: Adoption should not await winning standardization. The preferred incremental sequence is comprehend one bounded source slice, publish one fragment, stitch an adjacent fragment, answer a painful question the incumbent cannot answer cleanly, and emit conventional/covariant outputs side by side. This does not demand immediate central convergence. Practical proof demonstrates legacy and richer covariant outputs from one semantic substrate; when sufficiently mature it should also demonstrate deterministic compilation preserving traceability and challengeability.

grounding.quote:
Use normative application specs where the problem is primarily:

- user interaction
- workflow choice
- non-domain behavior
- operational policy beyond the domain semantics themselves

Use the world model as the semantic substrate wherever the software is mainly
an interface over stable domain reality.

constraints.statement: World-model development parallels spec-driven development: specifications are usually normative and models usually descriptive.
